Nine engagements, and not one of them started with the model.

That is my whole history of doing this, in my own time tracking, and I checked
it because I was about to write the opposite. I would have told you that the
first thing a fractional CFO does is open the spreadsheet. It is the thing I am
paid for and it is the thing I am best at, so it is the thing I assumed I did.

What actually happens in the first two weeks is that I read. The last three
board packs, the last two investor updates, the contracts for the largest three
customers, and whatever thread the founder and their lead investor have been
having about hiring. None of that is finance. All of it decides what the model
has to answer.

The founders who get the most out of me are the ones who arrive at the first
call already knowing which decision is stuck. Not with a clean model. With a
decision.

So here is the thing worth doing before you hire anybody, me included. Write
down the three decisions your next two quarters turn on, in one sentence each,
and note who has to agree for each one to be made. If the list is easy, you do
not need a CFO yet. If you cannot finish it, that is the engagement, and the
model comes second.

There are four questions I use to get that list out of a founder in twenty
minutes. If you want them, say so and I will send them. They cost nothing and
they are not a funnel.

Nadia Feriel, fractional CFO for seed and Series A B2B SaaS.
I build the model and I sit in the room when it gets argued about.
